question: A 66-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after the abrupt onset of painless loss of vision in his left eye. Over the last several years, he has noticed increased blurring of vision; he says the blurring has made it difficult to read, but he can read better if he holds the book below or above eye level. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. Fundoscopic examination shows subretinal fluid and small hemorrhage with grayish-green discoloration in the macular area in the left eye, and multiple drusen in the right eye with retinal pigment epithelial changes. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient's eye condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Smoking -> Increased risk of eye conditions -> Macular degeneration -> 70% CHAIN: Blurred vision -> Difficulty reading -> Macular degeneration -> 60% CHAIN: Subretinal fluid and hemorrhage in left eye -> Macular degeneration -> 80% CHAIN: Drusen and retinal pigment epithelial changes in right eye -> Age-related macular degeneration -> 90% CHAIN: Macular degeneration -> Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) overexpression -> Ranibizumab -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with painless loss of vision in the left eye, subretinal fluid, hemorrhage, and drusen in the right eye is consistent with age-related macular degeneration. The most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this condition is Ranibizumab, which targets vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) overexpression associated with macular degeneration.
analysis: The patient's presentation with painless loss of vision, subretinal fluid, hemorrhage, and drusen is indicative of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Ranibizumab, which targets vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) overexpression associated with AMD, is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this condition based on consensus guidelines.
